title: SOC 2 on AWS
subtitle: From service commitments to tested controls and defensible evidence.
label: A complete learning and assurance-engineering case study
disclosure: Fictional SaaS service, synthetic records and illustrative management workpapers. No real customer data, production AWS deployment, CPA examination or issued SOC 2 report is represented.

controls.title: Accountability and independent oversight
controls.population: Service leadership, control owners, oversight meetings
controls.risk: Controls can be bypassed when responsibilities and escalation rights are unclear.
controls.implementation: Approve an ethics policy, accountability matrix, delegated authority and independent oversight charter. Assign a primary and backup for every control.
controls.designTest: Inspect approval authority and conflicts between operator, reviewer and risk acceptor.
controls.operatingTest: Inspect each quarterly oversight packet and trace overdue issues to decisions and follow-up.
controls.limits: AWS account ownership does not establish organizational accountability.
controls.mapping: Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

controls.title: Workforce competence and security education
controls.population: Employees and contractors with scoped system access
controls.risk: Untrained personnel mishandle customer data or escalate incidents too late.
controls.implementation: Require role-specific onboarding, acceptable-use acknowledgement and security training before production access. Track contractors as well as employees.
controls.designTest: Confirm curriculum addresses data handling, reporting, privileged work and access termination.
controls.operatingTest: Reconcile HR roster to completion records. Inspect overdue training and approved follow-up for every missed deadline.
controls.limits: A completion certificate does not prove a person can perform an operational procedure.
controls.mapping: Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

controls.title: Commitments and customer communication
controls.population: Contracts, security promises, SLAs, notices and support channels
controls.risk: The system fails promises that engineering never received.
controls.implementation: Maintain a commitments register linking customer promises to controls, metrics and notification procedures. Approve changes jointly with legal and engineering.
controls.designTest: Trace each promise to a measurable system requirement and named owner.
controls.operatingTest: Inspect contract changes and a notification exercise; verify owners received changes before release.
controls.limits: A marketing availability claim is not evidence of delivered availability.
controls.mapping: Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

controls.title: Risk assessment with change and fraud analysis
controls.population: Service assets, threat scenarios, suppliers and planned changes
controls.risk: Risk treatment overlooks insider misuse, dependency failures or new data flows.
controls.implementation: Define objectives and risk thresholds. Assess inherent and residual risk, including fraud and tenant isolation. Reassess after expansion, acquisition or incidents.
controls.designTest: Inspect scoring rules and scenario coverage; trace high risks to treatment owners.
controls.operatingTest: Inspect the approved assessment, change-triggered reassessments and treatment follow-through.
controls.limits: Risk scoring is a prioritization convention, not a calculated probability of loss.
controls.mapping: Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

controls.title: Independent controls evaluation and issue escalation
controls.population: All scoped controls and outstanding findings
controls.risk: The dashboard appears healthy while control evidence is absent or unreliable.
controls.implementation: Review control design, test results, unknowns and aging issues independently of operation. Escalate repeated deficiencies to oversight.
controls.designTest: Confirm review criteria, escalation triggers and reviewer independence.
controls.operatingTest: Trace monthly review decisions to evidence, tickets and independently verified closure.
controls.limits: A native compliance score excludes human controls and unrecorded resources.
controls.mapping: Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

controls.title: Policies, procedures and control versioning
controls.population: Policies, operating runbooks and automated test definitions
controls.risk: A documented objective has no executable procedure or deployed enforcement.
controls.implementation: Version policy requirements, operating procedures and test parameters together. Approve substantive changes and communicate effective dates.
controls.designTest: Walk a requirement from policy to operator instructions and technology enforcement.
controls.operatingTest: Inspect policy reviews and change records; verify the effective version matches tested operation.
controls.limits: Publishing a policy alone cannot demonstrate that it operated.
controls.mapping: Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

controls.title: Federated identity and MFA enforcement
controls.population: Workforce identities, Identity Center assignments and emergency IAM users
controls.risk: Stolen credentials allow privileged access.
controls.implementation: Use an identity provider with MFA and conditional access, IAM Identity Center permission sets and short-lived role sessions. Maintain separately monitored emergency access.
controls.designTest: Review IdP enforcement, bypass paths, permission sets and session duration. Test denied and allowed logins in a sandbox.
controls.operatingTest: Correlate sign-in records, role assumptions and exception approvals across the period.
controls.limits: IAM credential reports omit federated users. A missing aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent value does not establish missing MFA for federation.
controls.mapping: Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

controls.title: Least privilege and access recertification
controls.population: Human assignments, service roles, trust policies and resource grants
controls.risk: Accumulated privilege enables data theft or unauthorized changes.
controls.implementation: Grant job-based permission sets and narrow workload roles. Review identity policies together with resource policies, trust, session policies, boundaries and organization restrictions.
controls.designTest: Test representative effective-access paths including cross-account assumptions and explicit denies.
controls.operatingTest: Reconcile assignments to HR and role inventory. Inspect each review decision and evidence that revoked grants were removed.
controls.limits: SCPs and permission boundaries limit grants; neither grants permissions. Policy simulations need context and do not prove every runtime path.
controls.mapping: Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

controls.title: Privileged and emergency access
controls.population: Root principals, privileged sessions and emergency credentials
controls.risk: Unreviewed root use bypasses routine separation of duties.
controls.implementation: Remove root access keys, protect emergency identities with MFA, prohibit routine root work, require approval and alert on privileged use. Evaluate centralized root management where appropriate.
controls.designTest: Inspect custody, approval, monitoring and emergency recovery procedures.
controls.operatingTest: Trace every emergency use to justification, approval, session logs and after-action review.
controls.limits: A root MFA screenshot cannot demonstrate that privileged use was reviewed.
controls.mapping: Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

controls.title: Leaver access removal across every access path
controls.population: HR terminations joined to IdP, cloud assignments, IAM credentials and active sessions
controls.risk: A departed worker retains usable access.
controls.implementation: Set a one-hour lab SLA for all access paths. Disable IdP login, remove assignments, address active role sessions and native keys, and record final effective-access removal time.
controls.designTest: Inspect joins, immutable HR identifiers, time zones, retry handling and orphan-account detection.
controls.operatingTest: Evaluate all terminations against access-path exports. Investigate missing joins and late removal; independently retest each path.
controls.limits: The executable check evaluates supplied final-removal timestamps. It does not query HR or revoke access. Identity Center logout alone does not end existing IAM role sessions.
controls.mapping: Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

controls.title: Workload identity and secret lifecycle
controls.population: Runtime roles, CI identities, secrets and trust relationships
controls.risk: Long-lived build secrets or broad trust let attackers assume production roles.
controls.implementation: Use ECS task roles and OIDC federation for CI. Constrain audience, repository and environment subjects. Store secrets in Secrets Manager and verify rotation consumers.
controls.designTest: Review role trust, secrets access, rotation design and prod/nonprod isolation.
controls.operatingTest: Inspect role use, denied federation tests and successful rotation exercises without exposing secret values.
controls.limits: No static access key does not imply a narrowly scoped role.
controls.mapping: Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

controls.title: S3 public-access prevention
controls.population: Customer-data buckets and documented public delivery buckets
controls.risk: Public access exposes customer content.
controls.implementation: Apply account and bucket public-access blocks, minimize resource policies, disable unnecessary ACLs and review access points and cross-account grants. Keep approved public delivery separate.
controls.designTest: Inspect effective policies, account settings and alternate access paths against classification.
controls.operatingTest: Reconcile bucket inventory to current Config public-read results, investigate every exception and test external access safely.
controls.limits: The live collector supports public-read prevention only. It does not test public write, tenant authorization or every access point.
controls.mapping: Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

controls.title: Encryption and key governance
controls.population: S3 objects, RDS storage, EBS volumes and relevant KMS keys
controls.risk: Sensitive data or cryptographic keys become accessible to unauthorized parties.
controls.implementation: Use customer-managed KMS keys where the data policy requires them. Review key policies, grants, deletion controls and rotation eligibility. Check existing objects as well as bucket defaults.
controls.designTest: Verify key access separation, service integration and rotation strategy for the specific key type.
controls.operatingTest: Inspect key changes and denied-use tests; reconcile object inventory to required encryption and key IDs.
controls.limits: S3 encrypts new uploads by default. Bucket default SSE-KMS does not re-encrypt old objects; encryption headers and service delivery paths require deliberate design.
controls.mapping: Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

controls.title: Transport protection and network boundaries
controls.population: Public endpoints, VPC paths, database connections and external transfers
controls.risk: Traffic is intercepted or untrusted networks reach sensitive services.
controls.implementation: Require HTTPS at public ingress, private application/database subnets, restrictive security groups and scoped endpoints. Enforce database TLS and controlled egress.
controls.designTest: Review path diagrams, endpoint policies, listener settings and TLS clients.
controls.operatingTest: Test blocked paths and plaintext requests; inspect rule changes and certificate renewal evidence.
controls.limits: A private subnet does not by itself prevent exfiltration or enforce tenant isolation.
controls.mapping: Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

controls.title: Confidential data retention and disposal
controls.population: Customer content, replicas, logs, exports, backups and keys
controls.risk: Data persists beyond agreed retention or disposal destroys required evidence.
controls.implementation: Maintain classification and retention rules. Track deletion through replicas and backup expiration, apply legal-hold exceptions and document custody for physical disposal inherited from AWS.
controls.designTest: Inspect deletion paths, retention conflicts and customer commitments.
controls.operatingTest: Trace selected deletion events to application records, storage changes and backup expiration; verify legal holds are authorized.
controls.limits: Deleting a live object does not delete older versions, locked evidence or backup copies.
controls.mapping: Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

controls.title: Tenant isolation and data-flow authorization
controls.population: API routes, worker jobs, signed URLs and customer-data paths
controls.risk: A valid customer reads or writes another tenant’s content.
controls.implementation: Derive tenant identity server-side, scope every read/write, separate worker privileges and bind signed URLs to authorized objects. Document trust boundaries and data sinks.
controls.designTest: Inspect authorization design across ingress, application, storage, queues and export paths.
controls.operatingTest: Run cross-tenant positive/negative tests and trace a canary through application logs, CloudTrail data events and the evidence store.
controls.limits: IAM encryption controls cannot prove application-layer tenant isolation.
controls.mapping: Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

controls.title: Controlled uploads and data ingress
controls.population: Untrusted files, dependencies, containers and import jobs
controls.risk: Malicious content or unsafe components execute in the service.
controls.implementation: Validate types and size, scan untrusted content, quarantine failures and restrict execution permissions. Apply dependency and container scanning before promotion.
controls.designTest: Inspect bypass handling and quarantine isolation.
controls.operatingTest: Test rejected content and inspect scan failures, promotion decisions and dependency exceptions.
controls.limits: A scan enabled setting does not establish complete input coverage.
controls.mapping: Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

controls.title: Logging coverage and delivery integrity
controls.population: Organization accounts, enabled regions, required event types and log destinations
controls.risk: Actions cannot be reconstructed because events were never recorded or delivered.
controls.implementation: Centralize an organization trail, management events and selected sensitive data events in a log account. Enable digest files, restrictive access and delivery alarms. Record excluded events.
controls.designTest: Review account/region selectors, key/bucket permissions, digest handling and retention.
controls.operatingTest: Trace generated canary events end to end; check delivery errors, event latency, validation results and health alerts throughout the period.
controls.limits: CloudTrail event history covers recent management activity. A trail enabled result alone proves neither data-event coverage nor delivery.
controls.mapping: Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

controls.title: Detection and accountable alert response
controls.population: GuardDuty, Security Hub CSPM, application alerts and routed findings
controls.risk: Threat findings are generated but nobody assesses them.
controls.implementation: Define severity routing, owner acknowledgment targets and escalation. Feed GuardDuty and application detections to the response queue and monitor the routing pipeline.
controls.designTest: Generate safe sample findings and verify every expected destination and escalation rule.
controls.operatingTest: Trace the alert population to acknowledgments, analysis, dispositions and SLA breaches.
controls.limits: GuardDuty threat detection and Security Hub posture checks serve different purposes. Finding suppression is not remediation.
controls.mapping: Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

controls.title: Vulnerability management and verified remediation
controls.population: Deployed images, EC2 instances, Lambda packages and dependency inventories
controls.risk: Known vulnerabilities remain reachable in production.
controls.implementation: Use Inspector and build scanning; set risk-based deadlines that consider exposure and exploitability. Track exceptions with expiry and compensating controls.
controls.designTest: Reconcile deployed assets to supported scanners and verify deadline rules.
controls.operatingTest: Trace findings to patched deployment digests and fresh rescans; preserve aged and accepted failures.
controls.limits: A critical-CVE count ignores unscanned assets. A closed ticket without a rescan does not prove correction.
controls.mapping: Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

controls.title: Incident response and lessons learned
controls.population: Security events, incidents, communications and recovery actions
controls.risk: Teams fail to contain, notify or recover during an incident.
controls.implementation: Define severity, command roles, legal/customer communication, forensic custody, containment and recovery runbooks. Exercise a credential compromise with customer-data impact.
controls.designTest: Walk through escalation and decision authority including out-of-hours coverage.
controls.operatingTest: Inspect the incident population, a tabletop and actual remediation actions with verified completion.
controls.limits: Tabletop attendance does not establish that technical recovery succeeds.
controls.mapping: Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

controls.title: Independent approval tied to the deployed commit
controls.population: Production deployment events joined to PRs, reviews and immutable commit IDs
controls.risk: Self-approved or unreviewed code reaches production.
controls.implementation: Protect branches and release environments, require an independent authorized reviewer, bind approval to the deployed SHA and control emergency paths. Use OIDC for AWS deployment roles.
controls.designTest: Inspect bypass rights, approval freshness after commits and actor authorization.
controls.operatingTest: Reconcile every deployment to its exact SHA, approval before deployment, independent reviewer and successful required checks.
controls.limits: The executable test uses normalized exports. It does not query GitHub, check review dismissal policy or prove all deployments were exported.
controls.mapping: Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

controls.title: Infrastructure policy gates and drift
controls.population: Terraform/CloudFormation plans, deployed infrastructure and break-glass changes
controls.risk: Approved infrastructure differs from deployed state or violates a baseline.
controls.implementation: Review plans and apply policy checks for public exposure, encryption and logging. Pin tool versions, capture applied plan hashes and route out-of-band changes for review.
controls.designTest: Inspect rule coverage, bypass authority and false-negative fixtures.
controls.operatingTest: Trace plans to approvals, deployments and Config drift. Reconcile emergency changes to retrospective review.
controls.limits: A passing plan does not prove the live resource remained configured correctly.
controls.mapping: Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

controls.title: Secure development and dependency provenance
controls.population: Repositories, dependencies, images, tests and deployment artifacts
controls.risk: A compromised dependency or build produces an unsafe release.
controls.implementation: Threat-model major features, review code, run security tests and dependency scans, and promote immutable signed or verified artifacts. Restrict build role and repository administration.
controls.designTest: Review trust boundaries from source to registry to runtime and required security gates.
controls.operatingTest: Inspect release samples across teams and period; verify artifact digest and gate completion at deployment.
controls.limits: A signature authenticates a producer; it does not prove secure code or correct configuration.
controls.mapping: Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

controls.title: Backup coverage and protected recovery points
controls.population: RDS, S3 and other committed recovery assets across accounts
controls.risk: Ransomware or failure destroys both primary data and recovery copies.
controls.implementation: Map asset-specific RPO to backup cadence and retention. Use separate recovery custody, scoped permissions and cross-account/region copies where justified. Validate KMS access and protected vault policy.
controls.designTest: Inspect protected assets, failed jobs, deletion rights and recovery dependencies.
controls.operatingTest: Reconcile source assets to successful recovery points within approved RPO; investigate failed and missing jobs.
controls.limits: RDS Multi-AZ supports availability; it does not replace a recovery copy.
controls.mapping: Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

controls.title: Restore testing against RTO and RPO
controls.population: Scheduled restore exercises for each critical service and dependency
controls.risk: Backups exist but recovery misses customer commitments or restores unusable data.
controls.implementation: Restore into an isolated environment, validate application/data integrity, measure recovery from disruption start and measure recovered data lag against RTO/RPO. Record cleanup.
controls.designTest: Review test realism, start/finish definitions and required dependency validation.
controls.operatingTest: Compare each exercise to four-hour RTO and one-hour RPO lab thresholds; inspect application sign-off and retest late or incomplete exercises.
controls.limits: The executable test evaluates provided measurements and validation status. It does not restore AWS resources.
controls.mapping: Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

controls.title: Availability capacity and failover readiness
controls.population: Committed service paths, quotas, multi-AZ dependencies and capacity metrics
controls.risk: Capacity exhaustion or dependency failure interrupts the service.
controls.implementation: Set SLOs tied to commitments, monitor saturation and quotas, distribute critical paths across availability zones and document region-recovery tradeoffs.
controls.designTest: Inspect single points of failure, capacity assumptions and alert thresholds.
controls.operatingTest: Inspect load/failover tests, response to saturation alarms and measured restoration within objectives.
controls.limits: An architectural multi-AZ label cannot demonstrate successful failover.
controls.mapping: Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

controls.title: Supplier assurance and AWS report review
controls.population: AWS, identity provider, source host and critical monitoring suppliers
controls.risk: Inherited controls or supplier dependencies fail without a customer response.
controls.implementation: Tier vendors, review current SOC reports and contractual safeguards, identify report exceptions and map relevant complementary user entity controls to internal owners.
controls.designTest: Inspect service/region coverage, report period, scope and carve-outs.
controls.operatingTest: Review annual packets and follow-up; trace AWS user controls to the service’s own evidence.
controls.limits: AWS SOC 2 does not attest to this SaaS configuration. A bridge letter is a management statement and does not extend the audited period.
controls.mapping: Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

controls.title: Business disruption and dependency mitigation
controls.population: Critical supplier outages, key staff absence and communications
controls.risk: A supplier failure or staff loss interrupts service without an alternative.
controls.implementation: Document fallback, dependency recovery, customer notification and alternate operational coverage. Assess insurance and other risk-transfer choices as part of risk treatment.
controls.designTest: Inspect dependency scenarios, responsibilities and realistic fallback assumptions.
controls.operatingTest: Exercise a supplier outage and inspect actions to remove unworkable dependencies.
controls.limits: Risk transfer does not remove the need to meet the service’s own commitments.
controls.mapping: Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

controls.title: Physical responsibility boundary
controls.population: AWS facilities plus workforce endpoints and any customer-operated locations
controls.risk: Physical custody is assumed to be entirely inherited even for employee devices.
controls.implementation: Inherit AWS datacenter physical controls through relevant report review. Maintain endpoint inventory, device access, return and disposal procedures for workforce assets.
controls.designTest: Separate provider facilities from customer-controlled devices and premises.
controls.operatingTest: Inspect report review and selected device return/disposal records.
controls.limits: AWS datacenter assurance does not cover a contractor laptop.
controls.mapping: Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

controls.title: Evidence custody and data minimization
controls.population: Raw exports, test outputs, manifests and restricted audit artifacts
controls.risk: Evidence can be overwritten, detached from its source or expose customer secrets.
controls.implementation: Capture UTC observation/collection times, scope and logic hashes, raw response pointers and approvals. Store protected evidence separately from public synthetic examples; restrict retention and access.
controls.designTest: Inspect chain of custody, tamper detection, access restrictions and redaction method.
controls.operatingTest: Recompute manifests, inspect access history and trace output to raw input and reviewed logic.
controls.limits: A hash detects a changed file only if the manifest is trusted. It is not a signature or proof of source authenticity.
controls.mapping: Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

controls.title: Monitor the monitoring pipeline
controls.population: Expected collections by account, region, control and cadence
controls.risk: A stopped collector displays an old passing result indefinitely.
controls.implementation: Compare scheduled runs to an independent heartbeat inventory, alert on missed/failing jobs, monitor evidence age and reconcile expected to observed resources. Assign unknowns to owners.
controls.designTest: Seed denied APIs, truncated pages, malformed values and missed schedules; verify alarms and escalation.
controls.operatingTest: Inspect missed-run population, freshness results and recovery tickets; verify the detector still runs when the collector fails.
controls.limits: A job-success signal does not prove a complete extract.
controls.mapping: Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

controls.title: Processing completeness and accuracy
controls.population: Input manifests, processing jobs, outputs and stored results
controls.risk: A job silently drops, duplicates or corrupts customer records.
controls.implementation: If processing integrity enters scope, define accepted inputs, processing specifications, reconciliation totals, retry/idempotency and output/storage checks. Reject bad input and route discrepancies.
controls.designTest: Inspect completeness and correctness requirements at input, processing, output and storage boundaries.
controls.operatingTest: Trace input identifiers to output counts/hashes; seed duplicates, missing records and unauthorized transformations.
controls.limits: Checksums alone do not prove business-level correctness. This extension is outside the selected examination scenario.
controls.mapping: Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

controls.title: Privacy purpose, notice and choice
controls.population: Personal-information purposes, notices, consent and collection channels
controls.risk: Personal information is collected without appropriate notice, authority or choice.
controls.implementation: If Privacy enters scope, inventory purposes, define notices and lawful/contractual collection conditions, implement choice where applicable, and record valid consent decisions.
controls.designTest: Inspect notice/choice design and alignment with actual collection flows.
controls.operatingTest: Trace a personal-information collection to current notice, relevant choice and approved purpose.
controls.limits: Confidentiality protects designated information; Privacy includes obligations across the personal-information lifecycle. This scenario excludes Privacy attestation.
controls.mapping: Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

controls.title: Privacy lifecycle and individual rights
controls.population: Personal-information use, retention, rights, disclosures, quality and complaints
controls.risk: Individuals cannot exercise applicable rights and onward disclosures escape monitoring.
controls.implementation: Define purpose-limited use, retention/disposal, identity verification for requests, access/correction, third-party sharing terms, breach communications and complaint handling.
controls.designTest: Trace the lifecycle inventory to rights/disclosure procedures and monitoring responsibilities.
controls.operatingTest: Inspect requests, corrections, deletion/retention decisions, third-party authorizations and complaint resolution against stated deadlines.
controls.limits: This extension needs jurisdiction-specific legal review; a SOC 2 privacy scope does not establish blanket legal compliance.
controls.mapping: Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

controls.title: Asset inventory and scoped population reconciliation
controls.population: Accounts, regions, global-service identities, resources and owners
controls.risk: Unknown assets escape security controls and audit populations.
controls.implementation: Reconcile Organizations, approved region lists, workload inventories and service-native exports. Track owner, classification and lifecycle including retired assets. Review gaps before excluding them.
controls.designTest: Compare inventory sources and inspect discovery limits, permissions, pagination and global-service handling.
controls.operatingTest: Inspect daily differences and onboarding records; trace newly discovered and retired assets to required controls and disposal decisions.
controls.limits: Config only sees supported recorded resources. An inventory needs independent sources and explicit completeness checks.
controls.mapping: Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

glossary.definition: An independent CPA examination of a service organization’s described system and controls against selected Trust Services Criteria. A report provides assurance for an identified system, date or period, and scope; it is not a product certification.

SOC 1 concerns controls relevant to user entities’ financial reporting. SOC 3 is a general-use trust services report with less detail. SOC 2 reports typically serve informed, specified users under restricted use.

Type I addresses the system description and suitability of control design at a specified date. Type II adds operating effectiveness throughout a specified period and a description of tests and results. Neither replaces risk assessment.

One of Security, Availability, Processing Integrity, Confidentiality or Privacy. CC1–CC9 are Common Criteria groupings, not nine categories. This scenario selects Security, Availability and Confidentiality.
A criterion is an evaluation benchmark. Points of focus help interpret criteria; they are not a mandatory checklist of individual technology settings.
A specific action or mechanism that reduces a risk and supports an objective. State who does what, on which population, how often, what evidence remains, and how failures are handled.
The owner is accountable for the control; the operator performs it; the reviewer assesses evidence and follows up. Separate these roles where a conflict would undermine assurance.

Design asks whether a control could meet its objective. Implementation asks whether it was put in place. Operation asks whether it actually worked with the required consistency during the examined period.
The complete set of events, identities or resources eligible for a test. An access-removal test starts with HR terminations, not only successful removal tickets.
Selecting items from a reconciled population for examination. Selection depends on risk, frequency, reliance and judgment; there is no universal SOC 2 sample count.
Source information supporting a test conclusion. It needs relevant content, trustworthy origin, time coverage, complete population context and custody.
Prepared by client: documents and exports management supplies for auditor requests. A PBC index links request IDs to control IDs, dates, source and reviewer.
Information produced by the entity. Validate report filters, joins, pagination, date ranges, logic and record counts before relying on internally generated reports.

A deviation observed during testing versus a weakness in a control’s design or operation. Assess cause, extent and effect; neither a single exception nor a ticket count determines the audit opinion by itself.

A finding documents expected condition, actual condition, cause, impact and corrective action. Root cause explains the system failure, such as an omitted access path, rather than repeating the symptom.
A different measure that reduces a risk when the preferred measure is unavailable. Its actual coverage and operation need testing; an approval alone does not make it effective.
An authorized, time-limited decision to retain a stated risk with rationale and monitoring. It annotates a failure and does not convert the underlying test to PASS.
Management’s evaluation and preparation before an examination. It identifies gaps and builds evidence; it does not issue an independent SOC 2 opinion.
Management’s explanation of services, boundaries, commitments, infrastructure, software, people, procedures, data, dependencies and relevant controls.
Management’s signed claims about the description and controls for the specified engagement. Management owns the assertions; the CPA owns the examination opinion.

A provider performing part of the service, such as AWS. Under carve-out, its controls are excluded from the SaaS auditor’s testing; management still explains reliance and oversight. Inclusive treatment includes relevant provider controls in scope.

Complementary user entity controls are controls expected at customers. Complementary subservice organization controls are controls expected at a provider. The SaaS is a user of AWS and a service provider to its own customers.
A management statement addressing the interval after a SOC report period. It is useful contextual evidence, not an extension of the independent audit opinion.
AWS secures its infrastructure; the customer secures what it builds and configures. The boundary changes with the service, data and architecture.

An account is an administrative and security boundary. A region is a geographic service area; availability zones are isolated locations within a region. Define which are in scope and how global services are treated.
IAM defines AWS identities and permission policies. STS issues temporary credentials. Identity Center connects workforce access to account roles and permission sets.

An SCP restricts permitted actions for affected organization principals; a boundary caps an identity’s permissions. A resource policy controls access on the resource. Effective access depends on all relevant policies and request context.
CloudTrail records selected API activity. Config records supported resource configuration and evaluates rules. Events and configuration observations answer different questions.

GuardDuty detects threats. Security Hub CSPM aggregates posture findings and control checks. Inspector identifies supported workload vulnerabilities. Enablement is only the start of a response process.
KMS manages cryptographic keys and controlled key use. SSE-KMS is server-side encryption using KMS keys. Key policies, grants and data access need review together.
Recovery time objective is the tolerated time to restore service. Recovery point objective is tolerated data loss measured as time. A restore can meet one and miss the other.

Repeated tests with defined scope, fresh inputs, versioned logic, traceable evidence, failure routing and heartbeat checks. A daily snapshot provides observations; it is not automatic proof of uninterrupted effectiveness.
PASS meets the executable assertion using valid evidence. FAIL has a demonstrated deviation. UNKNOWN lacks enough reliable evidence. NOT_APPLICABLE needs a documented, approved scope reason.
OIDC lets a trusted workload obtain short-lived AWS identity from verified claims. Policy as code turns reviewed requirements into executable gates or detections with versioned rules and tests.

findings.condition: One termination retained effective access for 3 hours against the one-hour lab SLA.
findings.cause: The workflow disabled the IdP but omitted existing role sessions from the access-path join.
findings.impact: A departed worker could still access AWS resources during the gap.
findings.action: Add role-session handling, enforce short privileged sessions and validate every account assignment/native credential path.
findings.retest: Use a synthetic leaver with an active session. Validate denial on each path and final removal within 60 minutes.
findings.closure: Open in baseline; proposed fix and retest plan only. Original period deviation remains in the evidence.

findings.condition: customer-export has a NON_COMPLIANT public-read evaluation.
findings.cause: A migration copied a broad policy and had no post-migration access test.
findings.impact: Customer export data may be externally readable; configuration evidence alone does not establish actual disclosure.
findings.action: Remove the broad grant, enable required blocks, inspect access history and test read/write paths.
findings.retest: Obtain a fresh Config evaluation and an independent negative external-access test with the correct request context.
findings.closure: Open. Accepted risk, if granted, would remain a failing result.

findings.condition: deploy-03 used an approval for an earlier commit; deploy-02 was self-approved.
findings.cause: The release join used PR number instead of immutable deployed SHA, and did not compare actor identities.
findings.impact: Unreviewed changes can reach the production service.
findings.action: Bind approvals to exact SHA, require independent authorized review and close administrator bypass paths.
findings.retest: Seed a post-approval commit and a self-approval; both must fail while an authorized exact-SHA approval passes.
findings.closure: Open. A later successful deployment cannot erase the prior exception.

findings.condition: exercise-02 took 5 hours; exercise-03 recovered data 2 hours behind disruption time.
findings.cause: The recovery procedure omitted startup dependencies and used an insufficient backup schedule.
findings.impact: The service can miss its four-hour recovery or one-hour data-loss objective.
findings.action: Fix the dependency order and backup cadence, then repeat an application-validated exercise.
findings.retest: Measure from disruption start to validated service recovery; validate recovered-data timestamp and cleanup.
findings.closure: Open pending a complete exercise and independent review.

findings.condition: archive bucket evidence is stale; one expected bucket has no Config evaluation.
findings.cause: The team watched job exit status without reconciling the expected bucket population or evaluation age.
findings.impact: Two scoped items have UNKNOWN assurance even if the job succeeds.
findings.action: Add scope reconciliation and observation-age checks with independently scheduled alerts.
findings.retest: Drop an expected record and advance observation age past 24 hours; verify UNKNOWN and escalation.
findings.closure: Open; missing coverage is not treated as compliant.

questions.question: Why are CC1–CC9 not nine Trust Services Categories?
questions.answer: They group the Common Criteria. The five categories are Security, Availability, Processing Integrity, Confidentiality and Privacy. Group coverage is a navigation aid, not evidence that every criterion is satisfied.

questions.question: Can an AWS SOC 2 report prove this SaaS is SOC 2 compliant?
questions.answer: No. Review AWS as a subservice organization, confirm relevant coverage, and implement customer responsibilities. The SaaS management description and controls need their own independent examination.

questions.question: Does MFA enabled in an IAM credential report prove workforce MFA?
questions.answer: No. Federated workers may not be IAM users. Inspect IdP enforcement, bypasses and sign-in evidence, then correlate cloud assignments and sessions.

questions.question: What is the population for leaver testing?
questions.answer: All relevant HR terminations, joined to every access path. Starting with closed offboarding tickets omits the people whose tickets were never created.

questions.question: A daily collector returns zero failures. Is the control effective?
questions.answer: First establish scope completeness, evidence freshness, logic accuracy, expected schedule coverage and response to failures. Zero returned records or stale inputs must not become a passing conclusion.

questions.question: A deployed commit differs from the approved SHA. What should happen?
questions.answer: Preserve a FAIL for the release. Investigate whether independent authorized review covered the deployed code before deployment, and test the corrected gate with a post-approval commit.

questions.question: Backups succeed daily. Why test a restore?
questions.answer: A backup can be inaccessible, unusable or too old. Measure validated recovery time and recovered-data lag against RTO/RPO with the required dependencies.

questions.question: What happens to a failed result when management accepts the risk?
questions.answer: The failure stays visible. Record authorizer, rationale, compensating controls and expiry, and continue monitoring. Risk acceptance is not successful control operation.

questions.question: Is a file hash sufficient evidence custody?
questions.answer: No. It detects change relative to a trusted digest, but does not authenticate the origin or protect the manifest. Access controls, retention, source context and protected storage complete the custody design.

questions.question: How do you close a finding?
questions.answer: Fix the root cause, collect new evidence, run an independent retest against the original objective, and approve closure. Preserve the original result and impact on the examination period.

questions.question: What does one NON_COMPLIANT Config result prove?
questions.answer: A narrow AWS rule assertion failed for that resource and observation. It supports a finding but does not by itself determine the effectiveness of the entire control, criterion or audit opinion.

questions.question: Who issues the SOC 2 opinion?
questions.answer: An independent qualified CPA practitioner. Management owns the description and assertion; engineering and assurance teams supply evidence and remediation support.

guides.title: Foundations and beginner definitions
guides.content:
# Foundations and beginner definitions

Start with the distinction between a promise, a risk and a control. A customer expects content to stay private. Unauthorized access is a risk to that promise. A tenant-aware authorization check is one control. A denied cross-tenant request is test evidence. Encryption and monitoring add separate layers, each with its own limits.

SOC 2 describes assurance over a specific system. A tool score, cloud provider report or evidence bundle cannot issue that assurance. An independent CPA evaluates the description and controls for the agreed engagement.

## SOC 2

An independent CPA examination of a service organization’s described system and controls against selected Trust Services Criteria. A report provides assurance for an identified system, date or period, and scope; it is not a product certification.

## SOC 1 / SOC 3

SOC 1 concerns controls relevant to user entities’ financial reporting. SOC 3 is a general-use trust services report with less detail. SOC 2 reports typically serve informed, specified users under restricted use.

## Type I / Type II

Type I addresses the system description and suitability of control design at a specified date. Type II adds operating effectiveness throughout a specified period and a description of tests and results. Neither replaces risk assessment.

## Trust Services Category

One of Security, Availability, Processing Integrity, Confidentiality or Privacy. CC1–CC9 are Common Criteria groupings, not nine categories. This scenario selects Security, Availability and Confidentiality.

## Criterion / point of focus

A criterion is an evaluation benchmark. Points of focus help interpret criteria; they are not a mandatory checklist of individual technology settings.

## Control

A specific action or mechanism that reduces a risk and supports an objective. State who does what, on which population, how often, what evidence remains, and how failures are handled.

## Control owner / operator / reviewer

The owner is accountable for the control; the operator performs it; the reviewer assesses evidence and follows up. Separate these roles where a conflict would undermine assurance.

## Design / implementation / operation

Design asks whether a control could meet its objective. Implementation asks whether it was put in place. Operation asks whether it actually worked with the required consistency during the examined period.

## Population

The complete set of events, identities or resources eligible for a test. An access-removal test starts with HR terminations, not only successful removal tickets.

## Sampling

Selecting items from a reconciled population for examination. Selection depends on risk, frequency, reliance and judgment; there is no universal SOC 2 sample count.

## Evidence

Source information supporting a test conclusion. It needs relevant content, trustworthy origin, time coverage, complete population context and custody.

## PBC

Prepared by client: documents and exports management supplies for auditor requests. A PBC index links request IDs to control IDs, dates, source and reviewer.

## IPE

Information produced by the entity. Validate report filters, joins, pagination, date ranges, logic and record counts before relying on internally generated reports.

## Exception / deficiency

A deviation observed during testing versus a weakness in a control’s design or operation. Assess cause, extent and effect; neither a single exception nor a ticket count determines the audit opinion by itself.

## Finding / root cause

A finding documents expected condition, actual condition, cause, impact and corrective action. Root cause explains the system failure, such as an omitted access path, rather than repeating the symptom.

## Compensating control

A different measure that reduces a risk when the preferred measure is unavailable. Its actual coverage and operation need testing; an approval alone does not make it effective.

## Risk acceptance

An authorized, time-limited decision to retain a stated risk with rationale and monitoring. It annotates a failure and does not convert the underlying test to PASS.

## Readiness

Management’s evaluation and preparation before an examination. It identifies gaps and builds evidence; it does not issue an independent SOC 2 opinion.

## System description

Management’s explanation of services, boundaries, commitments, infrastructure, software, people, procedures, data, dependencies and relevant controls.

## Management assertion

Management’s signed claims about the description and controls for the specified engagement. Management owns the assertions; the CPA owns the examination opinion.

## Subservice organization / carve-out

A provider performing part of the service, such as AWS. Under carve-out, its controls are excluded from the SaaS auditor’s testing; management still explains reliance and oversight. Inclusive treatment includes relevant provider controls in scope.

## CUEC / CSOC

Complementary user entity controls are controls expected at customers. Complementary subservice organization controls are controls expected at a provider. The SaaS is a user of AWS and a service provider to its own customers.

## Bridge letter

A management statement addressing the interval after a SOC report period. It is useful contextual evidence, not an extension of the independent audit opinion.

## Shared responsibility

AWS secures its infrastructure; the customer secures what it builds and configures. The boundary changes with the service, data and architecture.

## AWS account / region / AZ

An account is an administrative and security boundary. A region is a geographic service area; availability zones are isolated locations within a region. Define which are in scope and how global services are treated.

## IAM / STS / Identity Center

IAM defines AWS identities and permission policies. STS issues temporary credentials. Identity Center connects workforce access to account roles and permission sets.

## SCP / boundary / resource policy

An SCP restricts permitted actions for affected organization principals; a boundary caps an identity’s permissions. A resource policy controls access on the resource. Effective access depends on all relevant policies and request context.

## CloudTrail / Config

CloudTrail records selected API activity. Config records supported resource configuration and evaluates rules. Events and configuration observations answer different questions.

## GuardDuty / Security Hub / Inspector

GuardDuty detects threats. Security Hub CSPM aggregates posture findings and control checks. Inspector identifies supported workload vulnerabilities. Enablement is only the start of a response process.

## KMS / SSE-KMS

KMS manages cryptographic keys and controlled key use. SSE-KMS is server-side encryption using KMS keys. Key policies, grants and data access need review together.

## RTO / RPO

Recovery time objective is the tolerated time to restore service. Recovery point objective is tolerated data loss measured as time. A restore can meet one and miss the other.

## Continuous control monitoring

Repeated tests with defined scope, fresh inputs, versioned logic, traceable evidence, failure routing and heartbeat checks. A daily snapshot provides observations; it is not automatic proof of uninterrupted effectiveness.

## PASS / FAIL / UNKNOWN / NOT_APPLICABLE

PASS meets the executable assertion using valid evidence. FAIL has a demonstrated deviation. UNKNOWN lacks enough reliable evidence. NOT_APPLICABLE needs a documented, approved scope reason.

## OIDC / policy as code

OIDC lets a trusted workload obtain short-lived AWS identity from verified claims. Policy as code turns reviewed requirements into executable gates or detections with versioned rules and tests.

Read [the AICPA resources](12-sources.md) alongside these original teaching summaries. No licensed criteria text is reproduced.

guides.title: Northstar Workspace system description and scope
guides.content:
# Northstar Workspace system description and scope

**Illustrative management draft, not a completed auditor-approved description.** Description Criteria are distinct from Trust Services Criteria. Management should validate this draft against the AICPA Description Criteria and actual system before an engagement.

## Service and principal commitments

Northstar provides a multi-tenant API to upload documents, process them asynchronously, store them and export authorized results. Customers choose tenant administrators who manage their users. Customer content is Confidential. Tenant metadata can contain personal identifiers; excluding the Privacy category does not remove privacy or legal responsibilities.

Scenario commitments are role-based access, confidential handling and controlled deletion, 99.9% monthly availability, four-hour RTO and one-hour RPO. These are teaching assumptions, not SOC 2 mandated numbers. Availability needs a defined measurement window, covered endpoints, approved exclusions and source metrics. Recovery applies to the core service and its dependencies, not only a restored database.

The illustrative Type II period is **2026-07-01 through 2026-09-30**. Management must identify material changes and relevant incidents during that interval and subsequent events up to report issuance. The lab's last-day snapshot is not evidence for all three months.

Selected categories: Security, Availability and Confidentiality. Processing Integrity and Privacy are optional appendices outside this scenario. Corporate finance and unrelated products are excluded. Source/build host, external IdP, cloud identity, deployment process, workforce endpoints and monitoring suppliers support the described service and must be considered even when they are outside AWS.

## Infrastructure and trust boundaries

Six fictional accounts separate administration, security, logs, production, nonproduction and recovery. IDs in the source data are placeholders. Primary region is us-east-1; recovery region is us-west-2. Global-service inventories are handled explicitly, with source and recording region identified.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Customer[Customer tenant] --> Edge[HTTPS edge and WAF]
  Edge --> API[Private ECS API with tenant authorization]
  API --> Objects[Customer S3 objects]
  API --> DB[Private RDS metadata]
  API --> Queue[Queued processing]
  Queue --> Worker[Scoped ECS worker role]
  Worker --> Objects
  IdP[External identity provider] --> SSO[IAM Identity Center]
  SSO --> Roles[Temporary workforce roles]
  CI[Source and CI host] --> OIDC[Constrained OIDC deployment role]
  OIDC --> Release[Approved release to ECR and ECS]
  API --> AppLogs[Redacted application logs]
  Roles --> Trail[Selected CloudTrail events]
  Release --> Config[AWS Config observations]
  AppLogs --> Logs[Log archive and security accounts]
  Trail --> Logs
  Config --> Collector[Read-only evidence collector]
  Collector --> Tests[Versioned narrow assertions]
  Tests --> Review[Owner action and independent review]
```

An application authorization boundary separates tenants. AWS IAM cannot by itself enforce every application tenant decision. Storage keys and resource policies separate permitted workloads; they supplement application authorization. Production and nonproduction have separate data and deployment identities. Recovery access has distinct custody and reviewed grants.

## Software, people, procedures and data

Software includes the API, asynchronous workers, database schema, source repositories, container images, release automation and evidence tooling. People include service leadership, identity/network/platform engineers, support, incident command, data owners, vendor risk and independent control reviewers. Procedures include onboarding/offboarding, access reviews, secure releases, vulnerability response, backup/restore, incident notification, supplier review and evidence custody.

Data classes include customer content, processing metadata, account assignments, deployment logs and restricted audit evidence. Trace each class through collection, processing, storage, export, retention, backup and disposal. Keep secrets and raw personal/customer payloads out of public work samples. Deletion commitments must explain older versions, retention holds and backup expiration.

## Provider and customer responsibilities

AWS is a **carved-out subservice organization** here. AWS datacenter controls are inherited subject to relevant report review; the SaaS auditor does not test them as if they were operated by Northstar. Northstar owns its application, configuration, credentials, permissions, selected logging, customer-data handling and monitoring response. For EC2, guest OS patching remains a customer responsibility; a managed service shifts some infrastructure work without transferring application accountability.

Review the actual AWS report through Artifact, under its terms. Confirm service and region coverage, period, opinion, exceptions, scope and complementary controls. A public SOC 3 report or logo is not a replacement for the restricted detailed report. Do not include restricted provider reports in this repository.

The SaaS is a **user entity of AWS**, but its own customers are **user entities of the SaaS**. Relevant AWS complementary user entity controls become Northstar responsibilities. Illustrative Northstar customer CUECs include managing tenant administrators, reviewing user grants, securing client credentials, configuring integration permissions and reporting suspected compromise.

## Before management approves scope

1. Reconcile account inventory to Organizations, include the management account and identify global services.
2. Reconcile services and resources to independent owner inventories, including unrecorded or unsupported Config resources.
3. Trace every contract/notice commitment to a requirement and control owner.
4. Validate every boundary and exclusion with product, security, legal and the CPA practitioner.
5. Record changes, incidents, data migrations and providers affecting the description during the period.
6. Version the scope and hash it into every evidence run. A scope change requires review, not an automatic adjustment of the denominator.

guides.title: Risk-based control design
guides.content:
# Risk-based control design

A catalog is useful only when its controls support the actual system objectives. Start with commitments, then threats and consequences. Record inherent risk before treatment and residual risk after tested measures. Use a documented qualitative scale; do not imply mathematical accuracy from a High/Medium label.

## R-01: Former engineer retains usable role-session access

Impact: Unauthorized access to tenant data. Inherent: High. Residual: Medium pending verified session controls. Owner: Identity operations.

Treatment: Join all access paths, address active sessions, and retest effective access.

Supporting controls: IAM-01, IAM-04, OPS-02.

## R-02: Customer bucket policy enables public reads

Impact: Customer content disclosure. Inherent: High. Residual: Medium pending policy remediation. Owner: Storage owner.

Treatment: Apply blocks, review grants, reconcile inventory and verify external denial.

Supporting controls: DAT-01, DAT-02, APP-01.

## R-03: Production release uses an approval for a different SHA

Impact: Unreviewed code enters production. Inherent: High. Residual: Medium pending release-gate correction. Owner: Release owner.

Treatment: Invalidate approvals on change and require the exact deployed SHA.

Supporting controls: CHG-01, CHG-02.

## R-04: Backup restores after the service deadline or loses too much data

Impact: Contractual recovery commitment missed. Inherent: High. Residual: Medium pending successful exercise. Owner: Recovery owner.

Treatment: Measure both RTO and RPO including dependent services and application validation.

Supporting controls: RES-01, RES-02, RES-03.

## R-05: Evidence collector loses a region but dashboard remains green

Impact: Unsupported management assertions. Inherent: High. Residual: Medium pending heartbeat and reconciliation. Owner: Monitoring owner.

Treatment: Alert on missing runs, missing identities and stale observations.

Supporting controls: MON-01, EVD-01, EVD-02.

## R-06: AWS or identity provider outage prevents service operation

Impact: Service interruption and customer notification failures. Inherent: High. Residual: Medium with tested dependency plan. Owner: Service owner.

Treatment: Review relevant reports and commitments, test fallback and communication.

Supporting controls: VND-01, VND-02, RES-03.

## A control specification before code

Specify objective, owner, operator, reviewer, population source, required frequency, evidence sources, parameters, failure semantics, remediation and limits. A criterion supports more than one possible control and a control may contribute to several criteria. Record rationale and which parts remain untested. Reuse evidence across requirements only after assessing matching scope, frequency, objectives and population.

Worked chain: customer confidentiality commitment → departed worker misuse risk R-01 → IAM-04 all-path access removal → join HR events to IdP/cloud/native credential/session records → one-hour threshold → late removal finding F-01 → session handling fix → independent effective-access retest. This chain prevents a control from becoming an isolated technology checkbox.

The one-hour SLA is approved scenario configuration. A real organization must set deadlines from its risks and commitments, then maintain sufficient removal evidence. Tests never invent thresholds because a framework is present.

## Design, implementation and operation workpapers

Design: does every identity path have a removal method, source, join and failure escalation? Implementation: have those methods been configured and tested? Operation: did every relevant termination during the period lose effective access within the deadline? An on-time ticket does not prove that a role session stopped working.

For each automated test, assess the logic using seeded known failures and known valid records. Validate extracts and timestamps independently. Review code changes and operator rights. Collectors are privileged information processors: their own access, change control and custody must be assessed.

## Human approval and risk acceptance

Require an authorized acceptor independent of the operator where appropriate. Record the failure, business impact, reason, scope, compensating measure, expiry and review cadence. At expiry, retest or escalate. An approved exception stays visible in failed test results and examination-period analysis. Do not relabel a failed control as NOT_APPLICABLE simply to remove it from the score.

guides.title: Control catalog and AWS implementation/testing handbook
guides.content:
# Control catalog and AWS implementation/testing handbook

36 original illustrative controls. The selected scenario excludes EXT-01 through EXT-03; they teach optional category work. Mappings indicate contributions, not a full compliance determination. Each implementation describes a proposed design, not a claim that an AWS deployment exists.

## GOV-01 · Accountability and independent oversight

**Domain:** Governance · **Owner:** Executive sponsor · **Frequency:** Quarterly

**Supporting references:** CC1.1, CC1.2, CC1.3, CC1.5. Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

**Risk:** Controls can be bypassed when responsibilities and escalation rights are unclear.

**Population:** Service leadership, control owners, oversight meetings

**Proposed implementation:** Approve an ethics policy, accountability matrix, delegated authority and independent oversight charter. Assign a primary and backup for every control.

**Design test:** Inspect approval authority and conflicts between operator, reviewer and risk acceptor.

**Operating test:** Inspect each quarterly oversight packet and trace overdue issues to decisions and follow-up.

**Evidence:** Approved charter; RACI version history; Meeting minutes; Action register.

**Automation:** Human review.

**Limits:** AWS account ownership does not establish organizational accountability.

**Reference:** [AWS Security Reference Architecture](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/security-reference-architecture/welcome.html)

## GOV-02 · Workforce competence and security education

**Domain:** Governance · **Owner:** People operations · **Frequency:** At hire and annually

**Supporting references:** CC1.4, CC2.2. Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

**Risk:** Untrained personnel mishandle customer data or escalate incidents too late.

**Population:** Employees and contractors with scoped system access

**Proposed implementation:** Require role-specific onboarding, acceptable-use acknowledgement and security training before production access. Track contractors as well as employees.

**Design test:** Confirm curriculum addresses data handling, reporting, privileged work and access termination.

**Operating test:** Reconcile HR roster to completion records. Inspect overdue training and approved follow-up for every missed deadline.

**Evidence:** HR roster; Training export; Acknowledgements; Follow-up tickets.

**Automation:** Human review.

**Limits:** A completion certificate does not prove a person can perform an operational procedure.

**Reference:** [AWS Security Reference Architecture](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/security-reference-architecture/welcome.html)

## GOV-03 · Commitments and customer communication

**Domain:** Governance · **Owner:** Service owner · **Frequency:** Quarterly and material change

**Supporting references:** CC2.1, CC2.2, CC2.3. Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

**Risk:** The system fails promises that engineering never received.

**Population:** Contracts, security promises, SLAs, notices and support channels

**Proposed implementation:** Maintain a commitments register linking customer promises to controls, metrics and notification procedures. Approve changes jointly with legal and engineering.

**Design test:** Trace each promise to a measurable system requirement and named owner.

**Operating test:** Inspect contract changes and a notification exercise; verify owners received changes before release.

**Evidence:** Commitments register; Approved notices; Communication records.

**Automation:** Human review.

**Limits:** A marketing availability claim is not evidence of delivered availability.

**Reference:** [AWS Security Reference Architecture](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/security-reference-architecture/welcome.html)

## RSK-01 · Risk assessment with change and fraud analysis

**Domain:** Governance · **Owner:** Risk owner · **Frequency:** Annually and material change

**Supporting references:** CC3.1, CC3.2, CC3.3, CC3.4, CC9.1. Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

**Risk:** Risk treatment overlooks insider misuse, dependency failures or new data flows.

**Population:** Service assets, threat scenarios, suppliers and planned changes

**Proposed implementation:** Define objectives and risk thresholds. Assess inherent and residual risk, including fraud and tenant isolation. Reassess after expansion, acquisition or incidents.

**Design test:** Inspect scoring rules and scenario coverage; trace high risks to treatment owners.

**Operating test:** Inspect the approved assessment, change-triggered reassessments and treatment follow-through.

**Evidence:** Risk register; Threat model; Treatment approvals; Change assessments.

**Automation:** Human review.
