**Reference:** [AWS Config rule evaluation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/evaluate-config.html)

## EXT-01 · Processing completeness and accuracy

**Domain:** Optional extensions · **Owner:** Data processing owner · **Frequency:** Every batch and release

**Supporting references:** PI1.1, PI1.2, PI1.3, PI1.4, PI1.5. Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

**Risk:** A job silently drops, duplicates or corrupts customer records.

**Population:** Input manifests, processing jobs, outputs and stored results

**Proposed implementation:** If processing integrity enters scope, define accepted inputs, processing specifications, reconciliation totals, retry/idempotency and output/storage checks. Reject bad input and route discrepancies.

**Design test:** Inspect completeness and correctness requirements at input, processing, output and storage boundaries.

**Operating test:** Trace input identifiers to output counts/hashes; seed duplicates, missing records and unauthorized transformations.

**Evidence:** Input/output manifests; Reconciliation totals; Job error records; Validation approvals.

**Automation:** Human review.

**Limits:** Checksums alone do not prove business-level correctness. This extension is outside the selected examination scenario.

**Reference:** [AWS Security Reference Architecture](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/security-reference-architecture/welcome.html)

## EXT-02 · Privacy purpose, notice and choice

**Domain:** Optional extensions · **Owner:** Privacy owner · **Frequency:** At collection and purpose change

**Supporting references:** P1.1, P2.1, P3.1, P3.2. Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

**Risk:** Personal information is collected without appropriate notice, authority or choice.

**Population:** Personal-information purposes, notices, consent and collection channels

**Proposed implementation:** If Privacy enters scope, inventory purposes, define notices and lawful/contractual collection conditions, implement choice where applicable, and record valid consent decisions.

**Design test:** Inspect notice/choice design and alignment with actual collection flows.

**Operating test:** Trace a personal-information collection to current notice, relevant choice and approved purpose.

**Evidence:** Purpose inventory; Notice history; Consent/choice records.

**Automation:** Human review.

**Limits:** Confidentiality protects designated information; Privacy includes obligations across the personal-information lifecycle. This scenario excludes Privacy attestation.

**Reference:** [AWS Security Reference Architecture](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/security-reference-architecture/welcome.html)

## EXT-03 · Privacy lifecycle and individual rights

**Domain:** Optional extensions · **Owner:** Privacy operations · **Frequency:** Per request; quarterly monitoring

**Supporting references:** P4.1, P4.2, P4.3, P5.1, P5.2, P6.1, P6.2, P6.3, P6.4, P6.5, P6.6, P6.7, P7.1, P8.1. Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

**Risk:** Individuals cannot exercise applicable rights and onward disclosures escape monitoring.

**Population:** Personal-information use, retention, rights, disclosures, quality and complaints

**Proposed implementation:** Define purpose-limited use, retention/disposal, identity verification for requests, access/correction, third-party sharing terms, breach communications and complaint handling.

**Design test:** Trace the lifecycle inventory to rights/disclosure procedures and monitoring responsibilities.

**Operating test:** Inspect requests, corrections, deletion/retention decisions, third-party authorizations and complaint resolution against stated deadlines.

**Evidence:** Rights register; Disclosure records; Correction records; Complaint monitoring.

**Automation:** Human review.

**Limits:** This extension needs jurisdiction-specific legal review; a SOC 2 privacy scope does not establish blanket legal compliance.

**Reference:** [AWS Security Reference Architecture](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/security-reference-architecture/welcome.html)

## AST-01 · Asset inventory and scoped population reconciliation

**Domain:** Assurance engineering · **Owner:** Asset owner · **Frequency:** Daily and on account onboarding

**Supporting references:** CC2.1, CC6.1, CC6.5. Supports the listed criteria in this system; partial, judgment-based mapping, not criterion equivalence.

**Risk:** Unknown assets escape security controls and audit populations.

**Population:** Accounts, regions, global-service identities, resources and owners

**Proposed implementation:** Reconcile Organizations, approved region lists, workload inventories and service-native exports. Track owner, classification and lifecycle including retired assets. Review gaps before excluding them.

**Design test:** Compare inventory sources and inspect discovery limits, permissions, pagination and global-service handling.

**Operating test:** Inspect daily differences and onboarding records; trace newly discovered and retired assets to required controls and disposal decisions.

**Evidence:** Account inventory; Regional resource exports; Reconciliation records; Asset lifecycle tickets.

**Automation:** API collection + human review.

**Limits:** Config only sees supported recorded resources. An inventory needs independent sources and explicit completeness checks.

**Reference:** [AWS Config rule evaluation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/evaluate-config.html)

guides.title: Automation lab: four narrow assertions with traceable evidence
guides.content:
# Automation lab: four narrow assertions with traceable evidence

The offline lab evaluates normalized exports. It does not claim to query HR, IdP, GitHub or AWS Backup. The optional live adapter reads existing AWS Config observations for customer-listed S3 buckets. It creates no infrastructure and performs no remedial action.

## 1. Establish the approved population

Inspect [demo-scope.json](../data/demo-scope.json). It lists 21 expected control/resource pairs, applicability, approved exclusions and parameters. Inspect [demo-snapshot.json](../data/demo-snapshot.json), which contains 20 observed records. A missing expected bucket is deliberately seeded. Populations are independent of successful results: starting from an API response alone hides records the collector missed.

All lab observations belong to the end of the illustrative July–September period. Freeze evaluation time at `2026-09-30T15:00:00Z` for reproducibility. Current-time evaluation will eventually make the fixture stale, as intended. `complete: true` means source export completion was declared, not that missing expected identities become compliant.

## 2. Execute and inspect

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python3 scripts/evaluate.py --as-of 2026-09-30T15:00:00Z --out evidence/local-run
python3 scripts/verify_evidence.py evidence/local-run
```

Results: 5 PASS, 8 FAIL, 7 UNKNOWN, 1 approved exclusion. Denominator: 20 applicable items; 5 / 20 = 25%. Unknowns stay in the denominator. There are **four executable assertion types**, not 36 fully automated controls. Use a new output directory each time. `--strict` returns exit 2 for failures/unknowns after writing artifacts; this is useful in a gate and deliberately fails the baseline fixture.

| Control | Executable assertion | Still requires independent work |
|---|---|---|
| DAT-01 | Current, conclusive Config public-read evaluation for each expected bucket | Full bucket/access-point policy review, public write, tenant access, population discovery |
| IAM-04 | Verified all-path removal within one hour of termination | Source extraction/join validation, active session handling, actual effective-access testing |
| CHG-01 | Exact deployed SHA, authorized independent approval before deployment, checks passed | Deployment-export completeness, branch bypasses, dismissed reviews, emergency process |
| RES-02 | Validated recovery within four hours, recovered data within one-hour lag | Real restore, timing source validation, dependency coverage, cleanup and sign-off |

Timestamps require a timezone offset. Boolean strings such as `"true"` are not accepted as proof. Duplicate identities or unexpected items invalidate extraction reconciliation. Scope hash changes invalidate the associated snapshot. Future/stale observations are UNKNOWN. Missing evidence is UNKNOWN; a demonstrated failure can survive a different missing condition on the same valid record. A missing global extract contract makes the run unreliable.

## 3. Build and validate a source adapter

For HR/IdP, use stable employee IDs and enumerate cloud assignments, native users, keys and active role sessions. For releases, use immutable deployment events and exact commit IDs, not just PR numbers. For restore exercises, capture disruption start, validated service recovery and recovered-data timestamp. Keep raw extracts and join diagnostics in restricted custody. Before production reliance, compare automation with a manual review and investigate every disagreement.

Known-fault tests exercise self-approval, old-SHA approval, late approval, late leavers, orphan access, bad timestamps, string booleans, missed resources, stale observations, unknown native states, independent RTO/RPO failures, denied APIs, repeated pagination tokens and tampered manifests. Tests prove those cases, not the entire service.

## 4. Optional live AWS Config collection

Use an existing authorized sandbox/account. Install only optional collector dependencies in a virtual environment:

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
python3 -m pip install -r requirements-live.txt
cp data/aws-scope.example.json data/aws-scope.local.json
```

Edit `aws-scope.local.json`: replace account ID, approved owner, region, exact Config rule name and expected bucket list. Validate scope independently; this adapter cannot discover your organization. The reviewed rule source is `S3_BUCKET_PUBLIC_READ_PROHIBITED`, configured and active for the intended S3 resources. AWS Config recording and evaluations must already exist. Review the proposed [read-only policy](../data/collector-policy.example.json) against current AWS authorization semantics and your environment. Wildcard resource scope here requires a role restricted to the approved account with no mutation permissions; do not attach broad administrator access.

Authenticate with your existing named profile, then collect:

```bash
python3 scripts/collect_aws.py --profile audit-read --scope data/aws-scope.local.json --out evidence/live-collection-001
python3 scripts/evaluate.py --scope data/aws-scope.local.json --input evidence/live-collection-001/snapshot.json --out evidence/live-evaluation-001
python3 scripts/verify_evidence.py evidence/live-evaluation-001
```

The adapter verifies the caller account, Config rule source/state and recorder health. It follows all continuation tokens, never filters away inconclusive native states and retains raw responses. For conservative freshness it uses the native ordering timestamp, which describes the source event or configuration snapshot that triggered evaluation; it also retains rule-invoked and recorded times. A denied read, missing rule result or unhealthy recorder is explicit collection-error evidence. Account mismatch stops collection; evaluation also verifies account and region on the snapshot and each record.

The evaluation bundle includes normalized input, scope, logic, JSON/CSV results and hashes. The separate collection bundle contains raw responses, normalized snapshot, scope, collector source, SDK versions and its own manifest. Verify both directories and retain both in restricted custody; the evaluation bundle does **not** automatically copy `raw.json`. Git ignores `evidence/live*/` and local scope files; inspect your outgoing files before publishing. The website embeds only checked-in synthetic evidence.

## 5. Seed a failure and prove correction

Copy the demo input and keep the original baseline. Change a correct release to a different approved SHA, evaluate into a new output directory and verify the specific FAIL. Correct the SHA and evaluate again. This proves a narrow logic transition. To close a real finding, an independent reviewer needs new source evidence and a test of the actual deployed control. Neither editing a fixture nor a later PASS erases the original period deviation.

## 6. Validate custody

Inspect `manifest.json`, then change a copy of `results.json` and rerun the verifier. Verification must fail. A digest is useful only relative to a trusted manifest. Store authoritative manifests under restricted access or signed/protected custody; local hash files alone are not source authentication or immutable storage.

guides.title: Evidence quality, population testing and custody
guides.content:
# Evidence quality, population testing and custody

## The evidence contract

Every result needs control/test version, scope hash, resource identity, state, reason, observation time, collection time and source pointer. Run metadata adds logic/input hashes, expected/observed counts and evaluation time. Keep source evidence and its report filters, not only a rendered green status. Retain original exceptions and later retests as separate records.

Observation time describes the source event or state being tested; collection time is when the export was obtained; evaluation time is when test logic ran. A newly collected old Config result is still old evidence. Config's ordering timestamp describes the event or snapshot that triggered evaluation, its rule-invoked time describes the rule evaluation, and its result-recorded time describes persistence of the result. The adapter retains all three and uses ordering time conservatively for freshness. Document which timestamp each assertion uses and why.

## Validate information produced by the entity

Validate scope filters, date/time bounds, pagination, joins, duplicates, row counts and report logic. Reconcile HR terminations to HR source totals; releases to the production deployment log; assets to Organizations plus service-native inventories; restore schedules to completed exercise evidence. Source exports that omit failures are not a complete population.

Validate account and region identity. A Config aggregator helps query recorded resources but does not discover unsupported/unrecorded assets by itself. Some global resources have recording-location considerations. Reconcile disabled regions, newly enrolled accounts and denied read scopes explicitly. Empty responses, timeouts and unexpected native states must be visible.

## Period coverage and sampling

The checked-in snapshot is **one observation at 2026-09-30**. It cannot prove three-month operating effectiveness. Build a control calendar and expected-run ledger. For daily controls, reconcile expected days/runs with collected records; for event-based controls, reconcile every eligible event; for quarterly controls, inspect the review and follow-through. Retain effective versions of policies, logic and parameters throughout the period.

For a worked manual access review, imagine 12 privileged users at quarter-end: reconcile all 12 to assignments and HR, check all reviewer decisions and validate the revoked grants. For an illustrative release walkthrough, select early-, middle- and late-period deployments plus an emergency deployment from a reconciled release population. **These are teaching selections, not an auditor-approved sample size.** The CPA determines sample strategy based on risk, frequency, control reliance, population and judgment. Automated full-population output still needs validation of source completeness and logic/change controls.

## Evidence storage design

A restricted log/evidence account receives raw exports and manifests; a separate reviewer role reads them. Scope prefix/bucket/key policies, encryption rights and retention. Use S3 versioning and, where appropriate, carefully designed Object Lock retention. Governance and compliance modes have different override/deletion implications. Resolve legal hold, privacy deletion and retention conflicts before selecting settings. Prevent the operator from silently replacing accepted evidence.

CloudTrail integrity validation needs digest delivery **and actual validation**. Enabling the setting does not prove the chain was checked. Preserve validation output and investigate missing logs/digests. Log integrity does not demonstrate events that were never selected for logging.

Public examples contain fictional identifiers. Raw provider reports, credentials, personal information, customer content and live access details stay restricted. Review redaction without severing critical correlations. Keep source-to-redacted transformations reproducible and access-controlled.

## PBC index

[PBC requests](../data/pbc-requests.csv) connect request IDs to control IDs, period, source and review expectations. An auditor request tracker should also hold received date, custodian, restriction, version, reviewer, question status and links to the exact submitted artifacts. Never replace an old submitted artifact without retaining history and notifying the relevant reviewer.

## Readiness versus test conclusion

Show catalog controls, executable assertions, items observed, missing evidence, failed tests, approved exclusions and aging findings separately. A 25% narrow-assertion pass rate does not mean the organization is 25% ready, and a future 100% would not imply a clean opinion. Management assesses readiness using design, period coverage, evidence quality and unresolved risk; the CPA independently evaluates the engagement.

guides.title: Findings, root causes and corrective actions
guides.content:
# Findings, root causes and corrective actions

The five findings below are scenario examples. Severity reflects service risk and evidence context, not a universal SOC 2 rating rule. Multiple deviations can share a root cause; evaluate extent across the full population.

## F-01 · IAM-04 · High

**Condition:** One termination retained effective access for 3 hours against the one-hour lab SLA.

**Root-cause hypothesis:** The workflow disabled the IdP but omitted existing role sessions from the access-path join.

**Impact:** A departed worker could still access AWS resources during the gap.

**Owner / target:** Identity operations / 2026-10-15 (scenario).

**Corrective action:** Add role-session handling, enforce short privileged sessions and validate every account assignment/native credential path.

**Independent retest:** Use a synthetic leaver with an active session. Validate denial on each path and final removal within 60 minutes.

**Status:** Open in baseline; proposed fix and retest plan only. Original period deviation remains in the evidence.

## F-02 · DAT-01 · High

**Condition:** customer-export has a NON_COMPLIANT public-read evaluation.

**Root-cause hypothesis:** A migration copied a broad policy and had no post-migration access test.

**Impact:** Customer export data may be externally readable; configuration evidence alone does not establish actual disclosure.

**Owner / target:** Storage owner / 2026-10-08 (scenario).

**Corrective action:** Remove the broad grant, enable required blocks, inspect access history and test read/write paths.

**Independent retest:** Obtain a fresh Config evaluation and an independent negative external-access test with the correct request context.

**Status:** Open. Accepted risk, if granted, would remain a failing result.

## F-03 · CHG-01 · High

**Condition:** deploy-03 used an approval for an earlier commit; deploy-02 was self-approved.

**Root-cause hypothesis:** The release join used PR number instead of immutable deployed SHA, and did not compare actor identities.

**Impact:** Unreviewed changes can reach the production service.

**Owner / target:** Release owner / 2026-10-12 (scenario).

**Corrective action:** Bind approvals to exact SHA, require independent authorized review and close administrator bypass paths.

**Independent retest:** Seed a post-approval commit and a self-approval; both must fail while an authorized exact-SHA approval passes.

**Status:** Open. A later successful deployment cannot erase the prior exception.

## F-04 · RES-02 · High

**Condition:** exercise-02 took 5 hours; exercise-03 recovered data 2 hours behind disruption time.

**Root-cause hypothesis:** The recovery procedure omitted startup dependencies and used an insufficient backup schedule.

**Impact:** The service can miss its four-hour recovery or one-hour data-loss objective.

**Owner / target:** Recovery owner / 2026-10-22 (scenario).

**Corrective action:** Fix the dependency order and backup cadence, then repeat an application-validated exercise.

**Independent retest:** Measure from disruption start to validated service recovery; validate recovered-data timestamp and cleanup.

**Status:** Open pending a complete exercise and independent review.

## F-05 · EVD-02 · Medium

**Condition:** archive bucket evidence is stale; one expected bucket has no Config evaluation.

**Root-cause hypothesis:** The team watched job exit status without reconciling the expected bucket population or evaluation age.

**Impact:** Two scoped items have UNKNOWN assurance even if the job succeeds.

**Owner / target:** Monitoring owner / 2026-10-10 (scenario).

**Corrective action:** Add scope reconciliation and observation-age checks with independently scheduled alerts.

**Independent retest:** Drop an expected record and advance observation age past 24 hours; verify UNKNOWN and escalation.

**Status:** Open; missing coverage is not treated as compliant.

## Worked communication: executive briefing

**Illustrative 2026-10-03 review.** The 36-control catalog is documented, while four narrow assertion types have been evaluated over an end-of-period snapshot. Of 21 expected items, 20 are applicable: 5 pass, 8 fail and 7 lack sufficient reliable evidence. One approved public-document delivery exclusion is separate. Five findings remain open. These figures do not determine examination readiness or an audit opinion.

The main exposures are retained leaver access, potential bucket exposure, unreviewed releases and missed recovery objectives. Assign owners to correct the workflows and obtain independent retests; storage exposure warrants prompt investigation. Restore evidence coverage and the missing-bucket population before relying on dashboard summaries. Management should decide audit timing using the complete control/period evidence, not the last-day snapshot.

## Worked communication: engineering handoff for F-03

Expected: every production deployment has authorized independent approval for the exact deployed SHA before deployment, and successful required checks. Actual: deploy-02 shares deployer/approver identity; deploy-03 references an older approved SHA. Reproduce using the offline fixture and inspect the raw release join in the real source workflow. Replace PR-only joins, verify review authorization and prevent post-approval code changes from reusing stale approval. Retest normal, self-approved, changed-SHA and emergency paths. Preserve original events and inspect other affected deployments.

## Closure procedure

1. Confirm actual root cause with evidence, rather than treating the scenario hypothesis as a fact.
2. Record proposed action, owner, target, dependencies and compensating measures.
3. Implement under change control and assess whether similar resources/events are affected.
4. Obtain new source evidence and an independent retest against the original objective.
5. Record success/failure, reviewer approval and residual risk. Close only on supported correction.
6. Retain the original failure and evaluate its impact on period effectiveness; later fixes do not rewrite history.

For distributed teams, use UTC event timestamps and an explicit owner/backup. Leave handoff notes containing condition, evidence link, current blocker and next decision. A completed ticket is a workflow state; the retest establishes whether the control now works.

guides.title: Readiness and independent examination support
guides.content:
# Readiness and independent examination support

## Distinct deliverables and responsibilities

Readiness work identifies gaps, validates controls and prepares management. A Type I engagement addresses a specified date; a Type II adds operating effectiveness throughout a specified period. Duration, sequencing, sample sizes, report timing and opinion depend on the engagement. Type I is not an obligatory prerequisite for every Type II engagement.

Management owns the system description, selected commitments, controls and assertion. A qualified independent CPA practitioner determines examination procedures and report conclusions. Engineers and assurance staff supply accurate evidence, answer walkthrough questions and remediate issues. This repository provides management-side examples only; it does not fabricate a CPA opinion.

## System-description review scaffold

Use [the system scope draft](02-system-scope.md) as a starting point. Validate against the AICPA Description Criteria with your practitioner: service type, principal commitments and requirements, system components, relevant controls, boundary, incidents, changes, subservice relationships, CUECs/CSOCs and exclusions. The Trust Services Criteria evaluate controls; Description Criteria evaluate how the system is described. A well-designed control matrix does not complete the description automatically.

## Management assertion preparation scaffold

- Identify legal service organization, system, selected categories and date/period.
- Identify applicable Description Criteria and Trust Services Criteria.
- Support claims about description presentation and suitability of control design.
- For Type II, support claims about operating effectiveness throughout the specified period.
- Explain relevant carved-out providers and expected complementary controls consistently with the description.
- Confirm management responsibility, authority, known exceptions and material changes.

This is a preparation checklist, **not a signed assertion or licensed form**. Use the current practitioner-reviewed wording for an actual engagement. Do not sign a claim because automated configuration checks are green.

## PBC and walkthrough protocol

Give each request an ID, accountable custodian, scope/period, due date and restriction. Provide native exports and the validation workpaper. Walk through the actual process from trigger to completion, then show the failure path. For leavers, begin with HR events; for releases, begin with production deployment events; for backups, begin with the committed asset population. Track open auditor questions and clarify unsupported claims promptly.

Maintain a submitted-evidence log and freeze versions. If new evidence changes a prior response, preserve the old version and communicate the correction. Review access to restricted auditor portals and avoid public repository links for confidential source material.

## Supplier SOC report review workpaper

Record provider, service/region, report type, period, system boundary, opinion, relevant exceptions, carved-out dependencies and complementary controls. Compare covered period to your examination period. A bridge letter can add management context but cannot extend the CPA’s tested period. Map required user controls to named internal owners and actual test evidence. Determine whether gaps require additional work or a changed reliance conclusion with the practitioner.

Do not reproduce AWS's restricted SOC 2 report or claim that reviewing it makes the SaaS attested. Service coverage and report terms need verification for the specific account architecture.

## Report anatomy and follow-through

A SOC 2 report commonly includes the independent service auditor’s report, management assertion, system description and, for Type II, tests of controls and results. Additional organization-provided information may be presented separately with clearly identified assurance limits. Restricted use and distribution terms matter.

Distinguish individual test deviations from a modified opinion. Their effect depends on nature, cause, extent, compensating evidence and professional judgment. Discuss unresolved design/operation failures and subsequent events with management and the CPA rather than predicting the opinion from this project’s counts.

After issuance, retain the report and evidence securely, communicate appropriate scope/period limitations to customers, track complementary user responsibilities and independently verify corrective actions. Continue operating controls; report issuance does not freeze the system or eliminate ongoing obligations.

guides.title: AWS implementation and operational runbooks
guides.content:
# AWS implementation and operational runbooks

These runbooks describe proposed work in an authorized sandbox/real program. They are not executed by the repository. Record account/region, expected results, observed outcomes, operator and reviewer. Use read-only collection by default; perform negative tests and changes only where authorized. AWS services and data events can incur charges; this project provisions none.

## Identity and termination

1. Map workforce IdP identities to Identity Center assignments and permission sets. Include native IAM users, access keys, emergency identities and third-party access.
2. Validate MFA at the IdP and inspect bypasses. `aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent` is not a universal federated MFA signal; credential reports cover native IAM users rather than the entire workforce.
3. At a termination event, stop new authentication, remove assignments and address existing temporary role sessions and native keys. Existing IAM role sessions can survive the portal session.
4. Test whether each access path is actually denied and record the time effective access ends. Reconcile all terminated people against all paths, including missing joins.
5. Inspect the collector’s own access. Do not let a read-only evidence role silently acquire deployment or key-use privileges.

Effective access combines identity/resource policies, trust, boundaries, session policies and organization controls with request context. SCPs do not grant access and have important scope limits, including the management account and service-linked roles. Keep privileged work out of the management account and validate relevant exceptions.

## Logging canary: demonstrate how data reaches evidence custody

1. Enumerate accounts, regions and required management/data event selectors. Decide which sensitive S3 object operations need capture and record cost/volume tradeoffs.
2. Generate a unique non-sensitive object canary and a representative management event using an authorized test identity. Retain event ID, resource, actor and UTC trigger time.
3. Find the expected event in CloudTrail delivery, not just the console's recent event history. Verify selected fields survive normalization and redaction.
4. Trace delivery to log archive, Athena (if used), evidence collector, test output and protected storage. Record latency, missing fields and correlation IDs.
5. Test a broken route/permission in a sandbox and verify independent health alerts. A zero-row query without verified delivery is inconclusive.
6. Enable log-file digests where appropriate and actually run integrity validation. Preserve the result and investigate gaps.

Read-only diagnostic templates for an **existing scoped trail**:

```bash
aws sts get-caller-identity --profile audit-read
aws cloudtrail get-trail-status --name YOUR_TRAIL_ARN --region us-east-1 --profile audit-read
aws cloudtrail get-event-selectors --trail-name YOUR_TRAIL_ARN --region us-east-1 --profile audit-read
aws configservice describe-configuration-recorder-status --region us-east-1 --profile audit-read
```

The provided Config collector policy does not include these CloudTrail permissions; grant separately reviewed reads if needed. See [Athena query templates](../scripts/cloudtrail_queries.sql) and the documented schema/partition setup. Add partition predicates for your actual table. Querying root use or guardrail changes yields investigation leads, not automatic policy violations.

## Data storage and keys

Validate bucket and account public-access blocks, policies, ACL/Object Ownership settings and access-point paths together. The managed public-read rule is a narrow supporting assertion. Do not infer protection against public write or cross-tenant app requests from its PASS.

S3 encrypts new objects by default. If policy requires a specific KMS key, inspect object metadata/inventory as well as defaults and key policies/grants. A bucket default change does not retroactively rewrite existing objects. If you require explicit encryption request headers, assess integrations that rely on bucket defaults and log-delivery permissions.

KMS rotation strategy depends on key type and origin. Rotation does not revoke data access or solve compromised credentials. Review key administration, grants, scheduled deletion, recovery-key availability and access to encrypted backups separately.

## Release control

Join deployed artifact SHA/digest to source commit, authorized reviewer, exact approved SHA, required checks and release time. An old approval for the same PR is not enough. Test self-approval, late approval, changed commits, administrator bypass and emergency changes. Retain required status checks and environment approvals in addition to the source review. Constrain OIDC trust to approved repository/audience/environment claims and restrict the deployment role.

Policy-as-code gates should reject known-bad plans before deployment; Config-style monitoring detects post-deployment drift. Both need reviewed logic, parameter versioning and failure tests. Retain source, plan, policy results, approved artifact and runtime digest as a traceable chain.

## Vulnerability and incident handling

Reconcile running images/instances/functions to supported scanners. Prioritize by exposure and exploitability as well as severity, document deadlines and exceptions, deploy fixes and preserve rescans. A suppressed finding is not proof of remediation.

For a credential compromise exercise: capture detection and triage, classify impact, restrict affected access, preserve relevant logs, assess customer-data exposure, decide required communications with legal/management, recover with validated access and complete the after-action review. Test routing from GuardDuty/application signal to actual owner response and escalation. Do not stop at service enablement.

## Backup and recovery

Map every committed asset to recovery point cadence, retention, custody, key dependency and restoration procedure. Reconcile failures and missing assets. Multi-AZ failover and backup recovery address different risks.

Restore an isolated copy using approved procedures, bring up dependencies, verify application functions and data integrity, and measure time from disruption start to **validated service recovery**. Measure recovered-data timestamp relative to disruption start. Exercise loss of key access and an unavailable dependency, then record cleanup. AWS Backup restore testing can support job orchestration; application validation and commitment assessment remain necessary.

## Continuous operations calendar

| Cadence | Expected operation | Independent check |
|---|---|---|
| Per event | Termination, deployment, incident, sensitive-data disposal | Full eligible event reconciliation and completion evidence |
| Daily | Config/asset collection, backup and scanner intake | Expected/observed resource counts, freshness and heartbeat |
| Weekly | Alerts, vulnerabilities and failed/unknown results | Aging, assigned owners, actual corrective progress |
| Monthly | Control review, evidence access, capacity and pipeline health | Missing-run ledger, review decisions and escalation |
| Quarterly | Access recertification, recovery exercise, oversight | Population completeness, independent retest, approved action follow-up |
| Annually/material change | Risk, policies, training, vendor reports and boundary | Updated commitments, report coverage and design adequacy |

The calendar supports period evidence; it is not a mandatory SOC 2 schedule. Adopt frequencies justified by the system's risks and commitments.

guides.title: Category decisions and common-control reuse
guides.content:
# Category decisions and common-control reuse

This scenario selects Security, Availability and Confidentiality. Category selection follows service commitments and the engagement, not a desire to display every category. CC1–CC9 are common groupings, and the additional A1/C1/PI1/P-series criteria address category-specific objectives. Read the authoritative AICPA criteria when preparing a real engagement.

## Availability

Connect customer availability commitments to measured capacity, environmental protection, recovery assets and tested recovery. A1.1 concerns capacity; A1.2 contributes through environmental protections, backups and recovery infrastructure; A1.3 addresses recovery testing. The original catalog splits capacity, backup coverage and restore effectiveness to avoid equating a successful backup job with recovered service.

## Confidentiality

Identify information designated confidential, control access and transfer through its lifecycle, and dispose of it according to objectives. C1.1/C1.2 complement access and data controls. Encryption is one supporting mechanism; classification, authorization, retention and disposal remain necessary. Account for copies, object versions, backups and locked audit evidence.

## Processing Integrity extension

EXT-01 adds process specifications and reconciliations across information/input, processing, output and storage. Define what an accepted input is, what complete/correct/authorized processing means, how duplicate jobs are handled, and how lost outputs are detected. Trace identifiers and counts through queues and retries. Seed dropped, duplicate and unauthorized records. A checksum can confirm bytes while the business transformation remains wrong.

This is an optional design exercise; no pipeline attestation or automated Processing Integrity test is claimed here.

## Privacy extension

EXT-02/03 consider notices and choice, collection conditions, use/retention/disposal, access/correction, disclosures, quality and monitoring. A rights workflow needs appropriate identity verification without collecting excessive new data. A deletion request needs handling across the actual lifecycle and applicable retention requirements.

Confidentiality covers designated information; Privacy covers commitments for personal information. Omitting Privacy from a SOC 2 examination does not waive privacy law, contracts or customer promises. Legal review is needed for actual jurisdictions and rights. This project does not provide jurisdiction-specific compliance conclusions.

## Reuse without false equivalence

An identity removal record might support SOC 2 logical access, an ISO 27001 access-management control and a NIST access-control requirement. That does not make the entire requirements identical. Record mapping rationale, relevant clause/version, scope, coverage and remaining obligations. Test the internal objective once where appropriate, then review each framework's distinct requirements with qualified reviewers.

For example, IAM-04's timestamp check supports prompt access removal, but does not prove the completeness of access paths or the entire SOC 2 CC6.2/CC6.3 criteria. A policy or training criterion cannot be satisfied by reusing a bucket posture result. Avoid "one test certifies every framework" language.

guides.content:
# Learner workshop with worked reasoning

## Track 1: beginner, no AWS account

1. Read the foundations and explain SOC 2, Type I/II, criterion, control, population and evidence in your own words.
2. Open System & scope. Trace one upload from customer to authorized storage and logging. Identify application authorization versus AWS access boundaries.
3. Pick IAM-04. Explain its risk, owner, population, frequency, evidence and limits without mentioning a tool first.
4. Run the offline lab. Identify one PASS, one FAIL, one UNKNOWN and the approved exclusion. Explain why the denominator is 20.
5. Read F-01 and propose a retest that checks usable access, not a closed ticket.

Acceptance: you can describe the commitment → risk → control → test → evidence → remediation chain and identify who owns the management assertion and independent opinion.

## Track 2: assurance engineering

1. Copy the fixture; make deploy-01 approved at an earlier SHA. Expected: FAIL for that deployment.
2. Restore the correct SHA but set checks_passed to the string "true". Expected: UNKNOWN.
3. Remove customer-primary from records. Expected: UNKNOWN for that expected bucket, not a reduced population count.
4. Duplicate a record. Expected: the run rejects reconciliation and all results become UNKNOWN.
5. Set an observation beyond the evaluation time. Expected: UNKNOWN.
6. Change an approved threshold without updating the scope hash. Expected: snapshot mismatch, UNKNOWN run.
7. Keep recovery within four hours but move recovered data two hours behind disruption. Expected: RPO FAIL despite acceptable RTO.
8. Run manifest verification, modify a copy of an artifact and rerun. Expected: integrity check failure.

Acceptance: each output explains the exact assertion and limitation. Preserve separate baseline/fault/retest outputs rather than editing accepted evidence.

## Track 3: optional authorized AWS sandbox

Review an explicit account/region/bucket scope and named read-only profile. Use the Config collector against an existing active public-read rule. Inspect every raw page, expected/observed identity and native observation timestamp. Simulate a denied read with a restricted test role if authorized. Expected: collection-error evidence, then UNKNOWN in evaluation. Verify a newly collected stale native evaluation stays UNKNOWN.

Acceptance: a reviewer can trace normalized results to native input and confirm that no API error or missing page is treated as compliance. Live evidence remains restricted and outside the public site.

## Worked answers

- Baseline expected population: 21 items. Observed: 20. One missing expected item remains UNKNOWN. The approved public-docs exclusion removes one item from applicability, leaving 20.
- Narrow assertion pass rate: 5 / (5 + 8 + 7) = 25%. It is neither a criterion-coverage percentage nor a SOC 2 readiness score.
- Two leavers pass at 30 and 60 minutes. A three-hour removal and verified active access after the deadline fail; a missing final-removal conclusion is UNKNOWN.
- Release failures include self-approval, wrong approved SHA and approval after deployment. Missing approval and a string boolean are UNKNOWN.
- Recovery distinguishes late service restoration, excessive data lag and missing application sign-off.
- Closure requires new source evidence and independent testing of the implemented fix. A synthetic mutation proves logic behavior, not a production correction.

Use the interactive Review & practice section for additional explain-back questions. Answer first, then reveal the reasoning.
